solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: At first, say, regarded highly by following bot back (2,5,4)

indicatorNotes.back: reads BOT the other way round

blocks.note: with = following, as in 'are you with me?'

annotation.surface: Someone recalls being admired at first for trailing behind a robot, or a bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside, so the reversed bot leads the answer. 'Following' means understanding here, as in keeping up with an argument, not coming after.
annotation.definitionFit: To begin with and at first both introduce the opening point of an account.

entries.clue: Hedge trimmer — best one — is used in craft (9)

indicatorNotes.is used in: something used in a craft is put into it, so IS goes inside ART

annotation.surface: An advert praising the finest hedge-cutting tool on board a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat carrying the trimmer; it is ART, the skill.
annotation.definitionFit: A topiarist clips hedges and shrubs into shapes, so is literally a hedge trimmer.

entries.clue: Stay up late, hurtling wildly with him into bed (4,3,8,3)

indicatorNotes.wildly: the letters move about with no order

blocks.note: more anagram fodder, joined on by 'with'

annotation.surface: Someone crashes wildly into bed with a man after a late night.
annotation.walkthrough: The racy surface is a decoy: the eighteen letters of 'hurtling' and 'him into bed' rearrange to a phrase about working late.
annotation.definitionFit: To burn the midnight oil is to stay up late working, from lamps lit after dark.

entries.clue: Knight captured by regular attendee who doesn’t stand a chance (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a relative clause; read it as 'one who doesn't stand a chance'

indicatorNotes.captured by: a prisoner captured by guards is held among them, so N is held inside GOER

blocks.note: a goer = someone who goes, as in churchgoer
N = knight in chess notation; it sits in the middle of GOER

annotation.surface: A chess knight is taken by a regular player whose position is hopeless.
annotation.walkthrough: Knight is N, not K, because K is the king in chess notation.
annotation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed, who has no chance of surviving.

entries.clue: Not far from here, beat Normandy landings all the time (5,3,3)

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

annotation.surface: A veteran recalls a battle just down the coast and the Normandy invasion.
annotation.walkthrough: The break NIGH-TAN-DDAY cuts across the answer's word breaks, which hides it well.
annotation.definitionFit: Working night and day means working all the time, without stopping.

entries.clue: Anxious city needing cover all round (8)

indicatorNotes.needing cover all round: the city needs something wrapped all round it, so the word for cover encloses it

blocks.note: to insure = to cover against loss
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district; it goes after INS

annotation.surface: A worried town wants an insurance policy that covers everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like shelter for the city; it is insurance, which fits the anxious mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an insecure person lacks confidence and so is anxious.

entries.clue: Womanish urge to transform party (5-7)

indicatorNotes.to transform: to transform something is to change its form, so the letters take a new shape

annotation.surface: A feminine impulse to liven up a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like the thing being transformed; it is the definition, and only 'womanish urge' moves.
annotation.definitionFit: A house-warming is a party to celebrate moving into a new home.

entries.clue: Going too far, without any boundaries hence, from machine CGI (11)

indicatorNotes.without any boundaries: a word's boundaries are its edges, its first and last letters, so each word loses both

annotation.surface: A complaint that computer-generated effects have overstepped every limit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word, but it is fodder too: all four words after 'boundaries' are trimmed.
annotation.definitionFit: Encroaching means intruding beyond proper limits, going too far.

entries.clue: Tied 7-7, but first having added time (4-6)

indicatorNotes.but first: 'but' in its old sense of 'except': the first SEVEN comes without its first letter
indicatorNotes.having added: the second SEVEN has something added into it, so T is slipped inside

annotation.surface: A match finishes seven-all, but only after extra time is played.
annotation.walkthrough: The numbers are words to be spelt out, not scores: SEVEN twice, trimmed and then padded.
annotation.definitionFit: Even-steven means level, with neither side ahead, as in a tied game.

entries.clue: Slowly move animal’s stomach left (5)

blocks.note: a craw is an animal's crop or stomach

annotation.surface: An instruction to shift a beast's belly slowly to the left.
annotation.walkthrough: A craw is chiefly a bird's crop, the pouch in the throat, and is used loosely for any creature's stomach.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: babies and traffic both creep along at a snail's pace.

entries.clue: Ran faster than banned girl ran (11)

blocks.note: gal = girl, then loped = ran with long strides

annotation.surface: A race report: someone beat a girl who had been disqualified.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue says 'ran' twice: the first opens the definition, the second is LOPED, a loose-limbed run.
annotation.definitionFit: To outgallop is to gallop faster than, so outgalloped means ran faster than.

entries.clue: What separates firm teetotaller? No raised alcoholic drink (6,3)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top, turning NO round

annotation.surface: What sets a firm non-drinker apart? Refusing the gin that others lift.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hides that 'What separates' is the whole definition: a cotton gin separates fibre from seed.
annotation.definitionFit: A cotton gin is a machine that separates cotton fibres from their seeds.

entries.clue: Managed to support island nation (4)

indicatorNotes.to support: in a down clue, whatever supports sits underneath, so RAN goes below I

annotation.surface: Someone succeeded in backing an island country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island nation' reads as one phrase, suggesting somewhere like Fiji; the island is only I, and Iran is not an island at all.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Iran is one of the world's countries, found in the Middle East.

entries.clue: Meagre waif to a certain extent got bigger (4)

indicatorNotes.to a certain extent: only to some extent, so only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

annotation.surface: A thin child who, to some degree, filled out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a neat irony: the meagre waif is the one who filled out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to grow is to get bigger, in the past tense on both sides.

entries.clue: A working president (5)

blocks.note: per = a, as in 'twice a day'

annotation.surface: A description of a head of state who is actually busy.
annotation.walkthrough: Juan Perón was president of Argentina; the tiny 'A' does the heavy lifting as PER.
annotation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was President of Argentina in the 1940s, 50s and 70s.

entries.clue: Sign contract to cross southern river (7)

indicatorNotes.to cross: one word crossing another straddles it, so GET goes either side of S

blocks.note: to get (an illness) = to contract it
the Ure, a river in Yorkshire

annotation.surface: An instruction to put pen to a deal that lets you get over a river down south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sign' and 'contract' both look like paperwork; 'contract' is GET, catching something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a wave or a nod is a sign made with the body.

entries.clue: Wind up an affiliation surrounding jazz (9)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround is to go all round, so the word for affiliation goes round the jazz

blocks.note: trad = traditional jazz, the New Orleans style

annotation.surface: An instruction to end a partnership with a jazz club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like the verb to finish; it is the definition, a wind that blows up high.
annotation.definitionFit: An antitrade is a wind in the upper atmosphere, blowing above and against the trade winds.

entries.clue: Desert insect to bend with involuntary motion (9)

annotation.surface: An insect abandoning its post, curling up with a nervous twitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as a verb, to abandon; it is the noun. The Antarctic, with almost no precipitation, is the world's largest desert.
annotation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is technically a desert because it receives so little precipitation.

entries.clue: Country vet initially cutting side, in part going backwards (2,8)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so only the first letter of vet is used
indicatorNotes.cutting: a knife cutting food goes into it, so V goes into SALAD
indicatorNotes.in: the vet-and-salad piece is placed inside the part
indicatorNotes.going backwards: the finished string is read in reverse, right to left

blocks.note: a part in a play = a role
a side = a side dish, such as a salad
first letter of vet, which goes into the side dish; that piece then goes into the part, and all of it is reversed

annotation.surface: A vet in some country is first to trim a flank, then partly retreats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a dish served on the side. The reversal applies to everything, so build RO(DAVLAS)LE and read it right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is the smallest nation of Central America.

entries.clue: Crazy rumour said Ed cut bad form of proof (8,2,8)

indicatorNotes.Crazy: something crazy is disordered, so the letters lose their order

annotation.surface: A wild rumour claims Ed chopped a poor draft of the proofs.
annotation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase is a fair answer because the clue 'crazy' also nods at its meaning: reduction to absurdity.
annotation.definitionFit: Reductio ad absurdum proves a claim by showing its denial leads to an absurd result.

entries.clue: Old relative and daughter hugged by degree holder? (8)

indicatorNotes.hugged by: a hug wraps arms round someone, so the degree holder wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: d = daughter; it follows AND, and the pair sit after GR

annotation.surface: An elderly relative and his daughter are embraced by a new graduate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link word joining the two relatives; it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal word for a grandfather, a relative two generations up and so usually old.

entries.clue: Maybe Spanish river dropping temperature in gaining acceleration (7)

indicatorNotes.dropping: to drop something is to let it go, so the river lets go of its T
indicatorNotes.gaining: to gain is to take on, so IN takes A into itself

annotation.surface: A Spanish river cools and picks up speed.
annotation.walkthrough: The river is Italian, not Spanish; 'Maybe Spanish' is the definition, since Portuguese is Iberian too.
annotation.definitionFit: Iberian describes the peninsula of Spain and Portugal, so Spanish is one example.

entries.clue: Mate closely concerned with stuffing in bed (7)

indicatorNotes.stuffing: stuffing is packed inside something, so RE is packed into IN BED

blocks.note: re = about, concerning, as in memo headings

annotation.surface: A friend is closely involved in stuffing a mattress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a friend; it is the verb to breed, which 'in bed' suits.
annotation.definitionFit: Breeders use the term when they pair animals that are near kin, so 'closely' means closely related.

entries.clue: When driving, hit middle of tree with a tear (4-3)

indicatorNotes.middle of: the middle of a word is its central letters, so tree gives its two inner letters

annotation.surface: A motorist crashes into a tree and gets a rip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tear' can be a drop from the eye; here it rhymes with 'bear' and means REND.
annotation.definitionFit: To rear-end a car is to drive into the back of it.

entries.clue: Detective finally differentiates between characters of sea and of see (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of differentiates is used
indicatorNotes.between characters of: characters are letters, so S goes between two of the letters of the sea word

blocks.note: last letter of differentiates; it splits the sea word after its third letter

annotation.surface: A detective works out that 'sea' and 'see' are spelt differently.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sea' and 'see' look like a spelling lesson; one is OCEAN and the other a bishop's see.
annotation.definitionFit: Diocesan means of a diocese, the district that a bishop's see governs.

entries.clue: Stretch nearly worn-out hose? (7)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: a leg = a stretch of a journey

annotation.surface: A garden hose that is stretched until it is almost worn through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden pipe; the question mark flags the old sense, stockings.
annotation.definitionFit: Hose, meaning stockings or tights, is an example of legwear.

entries.clue: Hotel may have these horrendous debts, having acquired land (4,4)

indicatorNotes.horrendous: something horrendous is a terrible mess, so the letters of debts are in a mess
indicatorNotes.having acquired: to acquire is to take in, so the jumbled debts take the land word inside

blocks.note: to land a prize = to win it; it goes in after the first letter of the jumble

annotation.surface: A hotel in terrible debt has bought up land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotel may have these' is the definition, not the start of the story about money.
annotation.definitionFit: Twin beds, a pair of single beds, are a standard hotel room option.

entries.clue: Open up in merger, battling creature of 16 (7,7)

indicatorNotes.battling: things battling are thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A company opens up in the middle of a fierce takeover battle.
annotation.walkthrough: 16 is ANTARCTIC, the emperor penguin's home. 'In' is part of the fodder, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: The emperor penguin lives and breeds on the Antarctic ice.

entries.clue: Young, cute horse here at last (8)

indicatorNotes.at last: at last means at the end, so only the final letter of here is used

annotation.surface: A sweet young pony has finally arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Young' reads as describing the horse; it is the definition, and the horse is an old NAG.
annotation.definitionFit: Tweenage describes children of about ten to twelve, between childhood and teens.

entries.clue: Grind carbon into source of diamond? (5)

indicatorNotes.into: to put one thing into another is to place it inside, so C goes inside MINE

annotation.surface: Crushing carbon to make a diamond, since that is what a diamond is.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is science: diamond is pure carbon. 'Grind' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A kitchen synonym: meat put through a grinder comes out minced.

entries.clue: Artist’s publication in text lacking margins (8)

indicatorNotes.lacking margins: a page's margins are its edges, so the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: in text = WRITTEN, with its edge letters removed

annotation.surface: A painter's book is all text with no margins.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Artist is MAG + RITTE. René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist.
annotation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter.

entries.clue: Philosophical principle around cricket side deviating from course (6)

indicatorNotes.around: around means on every side of, so the principle goes on both sides of the cricket team

blocks.note: yang, the active principle of Chinese philosophy
WI = the West Indies cricket team

annotation.surface: A philosophy of cricket that has drifted off course.
annotation.walkthrough: Yang pairs with yin in Chinese thought; the longer YANG is needed here so it can wrap round the team.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship or plane is yawing when it swings off its straight heading.

entries.clue: Sent to accept promotion and allowed back in again (10)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so the word for sent takes AD inside

blocks.note: an ad = an advertisement, a sales promotion

annotation.surface: Someone sent away to take up a promotion is then let back in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a better job; it is an advert.
annotation.definitionFit: Readmitted means let back in once more.

entries.clue: Pressure inside bug’s eyeball (7)

indicatorNotes.inside: the pressure is inside the bug, so P goes into the insect word

annotation.surface: Pressure builds up behind an insect's eye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eyeball' is a verb here, and the 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal usage: to eyeball something is to give it a hard look, the verb built from the noun.

entries.clue: Removing flecks from miscreant ID, and ruffian in part (12)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective, 'for removing flecks from' the scalp; the answer is an adjective too

indicatorNotes.in part: the answer lies in part of the phrase, not the whole of it

annotation.surface: A police report about removing a thug's ID in part.
annotation.walkthrough: Twelve letters hidden across four words is long; the comma after ID is ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: An antidandruff shampoo removes the white flecks of dandruff from hair.

entries.clue: Entertainer twice almost got reindeer (2-2,6)

indicatorNotes.twice: twice means two times, so the trimmed word is written two times over
indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: GOT without its last letter is GO, taken twice

annotation.surface: A performer who nearly caught a reindeer twice.
annotation.walkthrough: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer, with Dasher, Prancer and Vixen.
annotation.definitionFit: A go-go dancer entertains at clubs by dancing energetically.

entries.clue: Progress banner? (2,5,4)

blocks.note: the surface reading: advancement, the cause a protest banner supports; the setter means moving forward along a road
the surface reading: a flag or placard; the setter means something that bans

annotation.surface: A placard carried in praise of progress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banner' looks like a flag; it is something that bans, and what it bans is progress down a road.
annotation.definitionFit: A no entry sign bans traffic from going forward into a street.

entries.clue: Enclosure next to first-class member’s lodge (6)

indicatorNotes.next to: next to means beside, so the pieces are laid side by side

blocks.note: enc. = enclosure, as marked on a letter
an MP = a Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: A fenced area beside a top Freemason's lodge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a building; it is the verb, to settle in a camp. The 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: an army that encamps for the night lodges there.

entries.clue: Part of nervous system in favour of cold beer mixed with spirit (11)

indicatorNotes.mixed: a mixed drink is stirred together, so the letters of beer are stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: Drinking cold beer with rum certainly affects your nerves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like mood or soul in a clue about nerves; it is simply the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this is the anatomist's name for the forebrain, which belongs to the nervous system.

entries.clue: Lecture succeeded without preparation (5)

blocks.note: s = succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A talk that went well even though it was unrehearsed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' reads as a noun, a talk; it is the verb, to tell off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a parent who lectures a child is telling it off.

entries.clue: Who gives advice on ugly acne needing treatment? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.needing treatment: to treat something is to work on it and change it, so the letters are reworked

annotation.surface: A question about who helps with bad spots that need treating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' belongs to the fodder, though it reads as 'advice on'. The whole clue also describes a typical letter to an agony uncle.
annotation.definitionFit: An agony uncle answers readers' problems in a magazine advice column.

entries.clue: Too hot brandy, perhaps what returned pub to profit (4,3,7)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a tot = a small measure of spirits

annotation.surface: Warm brandy was the thing that turned the pub around into profit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too hot' is a trap: 'Too' alone is the definition, and 'hot' starts the wordplay. EH? is how the British say 'what?'
annotation.definitionFit: Into the bargain means in addition, as well, too.

entries.clue: Heartless robber hits movie location (3,6)

indicatorNotes.Heartless: a word's heart is its middle, so the robber word loses its central letter

blocks.note: THIEF without its middle letter I
licks = blows, as in 'a lick of the belt'

annotation.surface: A cold-hearted thief turns up in a film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The flicks' is British slang for the cinema, from flickering film.
annotation.definitionFit: The flicks is informal British for the cinema, where movies are shown.

entries.clue: Lazy attempt to pen single article for Charlie Hebdo (4,4)

indicatorNotes.to pen: to pen animals is to shut them in, so the attempt word shuts in the single

blocks.note: le = the in French; Charlie Hebdo is a French magazine

annotation.surface: A half-hearted try at writing a piece for the French satirical magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing, which suits the magazine; it means enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: bone idle is lazy to the bone, completely so.

entries.clue: European agreed to prepare problem for viewers (9)

annotation.surface: A European agrees to set a puzzle for television audiences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' looks like TV audiences; here they are eyes.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness of the eyes, a problem for anyone looking hard.

entries.clue: Light vehicle tore around behind unopened supermarket (1-7)

indicatorNotes.around: turned around, the letters of tore are moved into a new order
indicatorNotes.behind: behind means after, so the jumble follows the supermarket piece
indicatorNotes.unopened: a word's opening is its first letter, so the supermarket loses it

blocks.note: TESCO, a British supermarket chain, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A little car races round the back of a closed supermarket.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain. 'Tore' is fodder, not a verb of speed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the electric kick scooters seen on city streets are among the lightest powered vehicles.

entries.clue: Weapons system is urgent, having started late (7)

indicatorNotes.having started late: a word that starts late begins one letter further in, so it loses its first letter

blocks.note: urgent = STRIDENT, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A weapons programme is pressing because it began behind schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: Trident is the UK's submarine-based nuclear missile system.
annotation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of Britain's nuclear weapons system.

entries.clue: Groups such as G9 ultimately have fun in the USA and Barbados (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so each following word gives its end letter

blocks.clueFragment: have fun in the USA and Barbados
blocks.note: havE fuN iN thE usA anD barbadoS

annotation.surface: A club of nations meeting for fun in America and the Caribbean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'G9' is a made-up summit name; nine is the point, since an ennead is a group of nine.
annotation.definitionFit: An ennead is a set of nine, so a G9 would be one.

entries.clue: Each piece of furniture is safe to put away (7)

blocks.note: ea. = each, as on price labels

annotation.surface: Every item of furniture can be packed away without risk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' means stored; it also means eaten, as in putting away a big meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Eatable means fit to eat, safe to put away in the stomach.

entries.clue: Pardon ugly dancing where one may be on the slide (10)

annotation.definition: where one may be on the slide

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers move all over the floor, so the letters move out of order

annotation.surface: Forgive clumsy dancing from someone who might be slipping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the slide' sounds like decline; it is the literal slide in a park.
annotation.definitionFit: A playground has slides, so a child there may be on the slide.

entries.clue: That woman’s raised sailor’s treatment (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: her = that woman; turned upwards gives REH

annotation.surface: A woman has brought up a sailor's cure.
annotation.walkthrough: Both 's are 'is', joining pieces and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A clipped form of rehabilitation, the course of treatment after addiction or injury.

entries.clue: Choose to garner support, hiding age in case anyone might see (4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: read as 'where a case is heard for anyone to see'; the definition is a phrase, the answer a noun

indicatorNotes.to garner: to garner is to gather in, so the choose word gathers the support piece inside
indicatorNotes.hiding: hiding its age, the support word keeps AGE out of sight, so those letters vanish

blocks.note: as written, and removed from the support word

annotation.surface: Choosing to rally support while keeping one's age secret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' is a legal case: a trial held in open court is public.
annotation.definitionFit: A case heard in open court is one that any member of the public may watch.

entries.clue: French novelist’s chapter delighted absent editor (5)

indicatorNotes.absent: an absent editor is missing, so ED is taken out of the delighted word

annotation.surface: A French writer's chapter pleased an editor who wasn't there.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Albert Camus wrote The Outsider.
annotation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist, author of The Outsider and The Plague.

entries.clue: Listen up, let’s spread covers (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' means reading from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.covers: what covers something hides it underneath, so the phrase hides the answer inside

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of let's into the start of spread, ignoring the apostrophe

annotation.surface: An order to pay attention: we will put the bedspreads on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Listen up' reads as one phrase; 'up' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Psst! is a hushed call used to get someone to listen.

entries.clue: Unoccupied, for example? (4)

blocks.note: the surface reading: empty, like a seat nobody is sitting in
the setter's reading: an example of the word, a country not under enemy occupation

annotation.surface: A seat, a room, or a country might be described as unoccupied.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unoccupied' seems to mean empty; the example in mind is a country not under occupation, which is free.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses meet: a vacant seat, and a nation liberated from an occupying army; the question mark flags the second.

entries.clue: Fairly harsh joke briefly upset model, breaking silence (9)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, a word is cut short, so the joke word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.upset: a cup that is upset is knocked over, so the model word is turned back to front
indicatorNotes.breaking: the two pieces break into the silence word, splitting it apart

blocks.note: to sit for an artist is to model; reversed
sh! = be quiet; the other pieces go between its two letters

annotation.surface: A rather cruel prank upset a model and shattered the quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' is the verb, SIT, not a fashion model.
annotation.definitionFit: Strictish means rather strict, fairly harsh.

entries.clue: Complain about Diana? (7)

blocks.note: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt

annotation.surface: Grumbling on the subject of Princess Diana.
annotation.walkthrough: The Diana is not the princess but the huntress. To chunter is British for muttering complaints.
annotation.definitionFit: To chunter is to grumble or complain under one's breath.

entries.clue: Channels to help, casually, those people from the east (5)

indicatorNotes.casually: in casual speech 'them' is clipped to 'em
indicatorNotes.from the east: on a map east is on the right, so an across answer read from the east reads right to left

annotation.surface: Aid channelled casually to people in the East.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal covers AID + EM together, giving MEDIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Channels, such as TV stations and outlets, are the media.

entries.clue: False doctor largely attached to wearing fur (11)

indicatorNotes.largely: largely means mostly, not all, so the doctor word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.wearing: the fur is worn round the attached piece like a coat, so ON sits inside SABLE

blocks.note: to doctor = to treat, without its last letter
on = attached to, as in 'a lid on a jar'; it goes after the first letter of the fur

annotation.surface: A fake doctor, mostly fond of wearing furs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to treat.
annotation.definitionFit: Treasonable acts are false to one's country, disloyal.

entries.clue: Sailors fear moments at sea (11)

indicatorNotes.at sea: to be at sea is to be confused, so the letters are muddled

annotation.surface: Sailors have frightening moments out on the ocean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' is the indicator, meaning muddled, though it fits the sailors' scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Foremastmen are ordinary seamen, who once berthed before the foremast.
